issue: BIO_QUOTE_FALSE_SALIENCE: a beep is not evidence of importance; use a distinctive tech boast rather than a misleading maxim.
text:
MIMI: I've got a plan! ...actually, wait, where's my phone?
LULI: Facts first. Opinions later. Snacks somewhere in between.
DILO: If it beeps, I can probably make it beep again.

issue: SUPPORT_COMMS_DRY_TAIL: replace generic tabs/battery maxim and doom with an actual family negotiation over the wall.
text:
DILO: I can fit all my theories on that wall.
LULI: And the evidence?
ALIO: We could put in a small shelf.
NINI: For the theories? Mine needs a cushion.
BIBI: Give it a question mark. I want to know which things we haven't proved.
MIMI: No cushions on the Case Wall. We are already one theory away from needing a bigger building.

issue: CASE02_FLOW: displaced blank-return details interrupt the question; reduce checkpoint jargon and give the missing handoff a clear narrative shape.
text:
That morning, Mimi crosses Trophy Hall with coffee in one hand and the other deep in her bag. Her phone appears to have taken the morning off.

The Founders' Cup has gone. That part is normal: Max signed it out for a Hall demonstration.

A few hours later, Dilo passes the display case.
"It's back."
Mimi stops looking for her phone.

The Cup is polished, centred and doing an excellent impression of a Cup with nothing to explain. Its return sheet is blank. No time. No signature. No handoff.

Bibi checks the tag clipped to the return record. One plain 0, just like the mark on the black envelope that brought you here. Nobody calls it a pattern yet.

One part of the demonstration record can still be checked: Max's location, and the one person who shared that room.
"Not a suspect," Mimi says. "Someone who may have seen it."

Was the Cup already back at that checkpoint, or did it return later?

issue: CASE05_PACING: make the dormant-locker activation a visible event rather than a sequence of repeated explanations of ignorance.
text:
Zuri's account repairs the handoff. Mimi routes the sealed evidence box back to the Trace Lab and files the correction.

Dilo's console flashes.

Under the Case Table, a dormant locker has linked itself to the current Academy session. That has never happened before. Behind its six-symbol panel is an old, sealed Academy envelope.

Dilo reads the screen twice. The locker has waited until a verified case was filed. Nobody knows why it has woken up, or what the envelope is doing there.

He looks at the keypad.
"One mystery at a time."

issue: SUPPORT_COMMS_REPEAT: setup must invite a human response rather than recite the pattern.
text: Four marks. One incomplete route. Does this printer ever send anything straightforward?

issue: SUPPORT_COMMS_MORAL_END: replace procedural maxim with sibling payoff.
text: You'd complain if it did.

issue: SUPPORT_COMMS_RELATIONSHIP: Nini joins the family joke instead of grading an idea.
text: Could it send something with a name? I'm running out of things to call 'the thing'.

issue: SUPPORT_COMMS_ACTION: Bibi has a concrete archive task and can answer the printer joke without supplying its meaning.
text: I'll take these to the archive. If it asks for me, tell it I'm checking its references.

issue: BRIDGE_OVERCLAIM: 'records it should not know about' suggests a watcher beyond observed system capability; retain ordinary reader belonging and the actual activation mystery.
text:
By the end of the first stretch of cases, nobody asks whether you are coming with them anymore. Mimi just leaves space beside the next file. Real staff have asked for help. Your filed answers have woken part of an old Academy system. It still has not explained why.

On the Case Wall, four matching marks wait beside an incomplete route. And beside the next file, there is room for you.

issue: CASE08_EARLY_ELIMINATION: the opener lists route eliminations before the task; show urgency and leave the actual choice with the reader.
text:
Zoe narrows the time when the moon costume went missing. She has not found the costume.

The rehearsal clock keeps running. The prop room is on the far side of the Undercover Wing, and Alio has drawn three routes to reach it.

They look beautifully quick on paper. Paper is less bothered by closed corridors and locked doors than people are.

Before anyone can check the prop room, you need a route that the team can actually use.

issue: CASE10_JARGON_AND_SHELL: replace human-overlap language with the concrete ownership problem and a clear witness question.
text:
Bibi goes into the archive with the true 0 samples.
"Records, not guesses," she reminds the team.

Ten minutes later, the Academy Science & Prototype Fair sends over a problem with two perfectly respectable pieces of paper and one inconvenient robot.

A Tech Lab mentor rolls a silver training rover up to the Case Table. Two students follow, each carrying an ownership sheet. Both sheets look legitimate. Both name the same rover.

Dilo crouches beside it.
"At least the robot seems calm."

The access log cannot settle which team had it during the disputed window. Dash's location is the last part everyone agrees on. Find the person who shared his area, and the team will have someone to ask what happened around the rover.

issue: CASE12_FORMULA: the handler query should sound like this bird interview, not another abstract last-reliable-placement explanation.
text: The rehearsal record puts Winter in one definite area. Who else was there? Find Winter's companion, and Nini will have someone to ask who won't answer every question with a snack request.

issue: CASE14_TRANSITION: retain the memory theme and coordinator's trigger without a narrator's 'more useful' evaluation.
text:
The camera was moved during cleanup, after the 4:17 frame. It did not move itself.

Mimi is still thinking about the two people who remembered those few minutes differently. Back at the Academy the following morning, the Scenario Theater coordinator overhears the discussion and puts four rehearsal statements on the Case Table.

issue: CASE15_FORMULA: make the witness's actual value clear through the existing bag-swap situation.
text: Milo's location is certain. One person shared his room and saw a backpack before all the helpful swapping began. Find that person, and the team can untangle who moved what.

issue: CASE17_FORMULA: use the physical ticket question instead of another last-reliable-point paragraph.
text: The station record fixes Reed's location. It also puts one person in that area with him. The ticket cannot tell you where it went next, or whether it was passed on deliberately. That person might.

issue: CASE19_FORMULA: reduce physical-side-of-digital-mystery abstraction; keep log and eyewitness roles distinct.
text: The log puts Sasha in one known location. Find the one person who shared that area. The librarian has a screen full of checkout data; what the file needs is someone who saw what happened beside the scanner.

issue: FIRST_INSTRUCTION_CONTINUITY: RULE 0 FIRST was already an instruction at80; qualify the fuller note and keep the reader's saved maps in the foreground.
text: The repaired note gives you more to work with than RULE 0 FIRST. It still refuses to say what to look at. Nini slides the growing stack of solved maps into your reach. Nobody asks whether you're keeping them anymore. Of course you are. If the old route wants something examined, you have a table full of evidence ready for it. Meanwhile, real cases keep arriving.

issue: CASE22_LOCAL_VOICE: another handoff query needs its own shelf/contents problem and natural reader-facing handoff.
text:
By morning, the repaired note is safe on the Case Wall. At Sound Lab, at least one problem can be put back on a shelf.

Three nearly identical instrument cases have been returned to the wrong shelves after rehearsal. Zara's location is the last certain point before the mix-up. One person shared her room and saw the cases before they were moved.

Find that person so Sound Lab can check the original shelf order. Keep the complete map too.

Mimi turns the file so you can read it.
"Shall we start with where they were meant to be?"

issue: CASE23_DUPLICATE_JOKE: one visual setup here; deliver the full scoreboard exchange at109.
text: Dilo glances at the arcade scoreboard. Luli opens the wristband file where he can see it.

issue: CASE24_MORAL_TAIL: carry Alio's observation into a human image instead of spelling out a general reminder.
text: The trail ends at the West Gate. Nobody walked backwards. Alio puts a small question mark beside the tread arrow on his tracking sheet. It was very sure of itself for something that pointed the wrong way.

issue: CASE25_WITHHELD_THOUGHT: Bibi should share the ordinary question raised by the visible label, not imply she is withholding an answer.
text:
Bibi reads ARCHIVE RESTORATION twice.
"If it belongs in the archive, let's find out who was meant to receive it."

issue: BRIDGE_COMMS_KEEP_CORE: exact Nini/Dilo two-turn attribution, verified from source layout, retained as a golden kernel.
text:
I knew we kept those maps for a reason.
I kept mine because the stack looked impressive.

issue: BRIDGE_COMMS_WARMTH: replace methodology verdict with sibling recognition and Bibi backing Dilo's useful filing.
text:
Two reasons to keep the maps. Yours is very you.
Useful evidence and an excellent stack. Let him have both.

issue: BRIDGE_COMMS_PAYOFF: end at the crowded family table, rather than a general wall-space observation.
text: Then let me have some table. My elbow has become a paperweight.

issue: INSTRUCTION_COUNT: the margin is another instruction, not literally the second after both photograph and torn note.
text: The old plan has its own instruction in the margin:

issue: CASE28_MORAL_TAIL: use the already-open evidence files and waiting wall to embody the need to test the exciting idea.
text: Mimi puts the old plan beside the tracking-yard file. The wall can wait until the team has checked what it thinks it knows.

issue: VICTORY_NOISE_CALLBACK: a simple family signal pays off the pending noise without restating the book's maxim at the reveal.
text: "Not yet."

issue: FINALE_MECHANISM_CLARITY: retain real cases, matching and conditional archive reopening in shorter natural clauses.
text: The cases were real. The route could match a current case record to an unfinished training step. When we verified that step, it could reopen the archive material for the next one.

issue: BELONGING_VS_CERTIFICATION: what the work earns is the field badge; the reader already has a place at the family table.
text: Only you could earn the field badge.

issue: FINALE_REPEATED_NEGATION: recognition of the reader's retained evidence replaces a third statement that nobody can fill the place for them.
text: And you have the evidence to fill it.

issue: FINALE_HUMAN_BEAT: keep the empty hook visible instead of explaining the invitation again.
text: "For your field badge," Bibi says, keeping the hook turned towards you.

issue: FINALE_PAYOFF: warm, concrete acknowledgement of reader work and the place the family kept.
text: "We saved the hook. You did the work."

issue: R1_NATIVE_MEANING: Jude is a person, not a place; make known location, companion and next witness question concrete.
text: The log fixes Jude's location. One other person shared that area. Find them so the return desk can ask where the two wristband trails crossed.

issue: R1_CHRONOLOGY: the earlier photograph already carried RULE 0 FIRST. This nonmechanic summary must call the repaired note a fuller instruction; all answer and physical-join text remains exact.
text: The repaired note gives the team a fuller instruction than RULE 0 FIRST. They still need to work out what it asks them to examine.
